subject: Production errors: 429 spikes, timeouts — customer impact (Venturi Health)
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@venturihealth.com>

Cc: ops@venturihealth.com
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Production errors: 429 spikes and timeouts — urgent

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in 429 responses and client timeouts across our API calls around 17:45 UTC. This is impacting our triage workflows and a handful of customer-facing pages. The errors started as intermittent 429s and escalated into a retry storm that knocked our page load SRE metrics into the red.

Attached: server-429-log-snippet.txt (extract), venturi-metrics-12-04.png (dashboard snapshot).

Immediate ask: can someone confirm whether this is on your rate limiting side vs something we changed? We did a deploy earlier today but it was a small change. Please advise how to get traffic stabilized — we may need a temporary quota bump if this is a Redwood cap.

Thanks,
Jamie Park
Lead Platform Ops
Venturi Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; Jamie Park <jamie.park@venturihealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 18:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors: 429 spikes and timeouts — urgent

Quick findings from the initial triage (logs + control plane):

1) We are seeing a sharp rise in 429s from our edge rate limiter starting 17:44:21 UTC. The pattern: many short-lived bursts from multiple project keys that belong to the same Venturi org id.
2) The org-to-tier mapping for Venturi shows two active projects. One project was recently moved into the new "flex-tier" during an automated onboarding job earlier today. The flex-tier has lower per-project rate caps but a different org-level cap aggregation rule (buggy config).
3) It looks like the automated onboarding job incorrectly set project scope to "per-project" rather than "org-aggregate" for the flex-tier policy, which caused our quota engine to enforce tighter per-project limits while still counting aggregate traffic against a low org cap. When many clients retried (backoff was insufficient), we got a retry amplification and the org cap started rejecting with 429s.

Immediate mitigations I applied at 18:39 UTC:
- Bumped Venturi org cap by +40% (temporary emergency increase).
- Disabled the flawed onboarding rule to stop new projects inheriting the wrong scope.
- Enabled a short-duration circuit-breaker rule to shed low-priority background traffic for 15 minutes to give production paths headroom.

Effect: 429s have fallen by ~85% in the last 10 minutes on our end. Jamie, please confirm whether you see improvement across your dashboards.

Next steps (short):
- We'll revert the onboarding rule and run a backfill to correct the scope for the misassigned project (ETA 24 hours).
- We'll publish a hotfix to ensure the flex-tier policy honors org-aggregate counting (ETA 48 hours).
- Marissa / Sean: I'll prepare a short RCA doc and logs for compliance.

Attachment: mutal-action-plan-v1.docx (placeholder — will update with timelines).

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Note: On the log snippet you sent, the client-side backoff is aggressive (0s retries), which amplified the retry storm. We recommend a client-side backoff change but I understand you control their client fleet.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@venturihealth.com>; Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production errors: 429 spikes and timeouts — mutual action plan

Jamie — glad to hear the immediate error rate dropped. Quick action items and timeline from CS side:

1) Temporary measures (complete):
   - Redwood increased org cap and disabled faulty onboarding rule (Aditya).
   - Circuit-breaker active until 09:30 UTC to reduce background jobs.
2) Venturi action items for the next 6 hours:
   - Identify the top 10 clients producing the most retries and push a client config to increase exponential backoff (Jamie / Ops).
   - If you want, we can open a temporary API key with elevated per-project limits for a control group while we fix the policy.
3) Redwood action items (owned):
   - Hotfix to policy engine to ensure flex-tier uses org-aggregate counting (Aditya) — ETA 48h.
   - Backfill correct scope to the misassigned project and validate (Aditya) — ETA 24h.
   - Customer-facing RCA and credits assessment (Sean & Stephanie) — initial draft 24h.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for 10:00 UTC to confirm the next steps and to walk through logs. Sean — can you confirm approval for a one-off elevated key? Jamie — do you want that or prefer the client backoff route?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
